newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan chooses JP Morgan to lead Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan chooses JP Morgan to lead Eurobond.

text.p: Kazakhstan's Finance Ministry said on Tuesday it had chosen JP Morgan Ltd to lead manage the former Soviet republic's $250-350 million Eurobond planned for September or October.

"The Finance Ministry announces its decision to mandate JP Morgan Ltd to lead manage Kazakhstan's future Eurobond issue on international capital markets and to advise on Kazakhstan's credit rating," the ministry said.

Earlier on Tuesday, the Finance Ministry's chief treasurer, Daniyar Abulgazin, told Reuters the oil-rich republic of 17 million would issue a dollar-denominated Eurobond with a maturity of five or seven years in September or October.
Kazakhstan is going to international markets to try and find cash to help pay off 36 billion tenge ($480 million) in pension arrears before the end of this year.
The Central Asian state issued a debut $200 million, three-year Eurobond last December, priced to yield 9.3 percent or 350 basis points above comparable U.S. treasury notes.

Moody's Investors Service last year assigned Kazakhstan a Ba3 sovereign rating for long-term foreign currency bonds while Standard and Poor's rated the republic BB-. Kazakh officials are hoping for a higher credit rating this year.
